# NAB FY25: Was B&PB growth value-accretive?

**Verdict: Yes, on balance.** Growth was broad-based, deposit-funded, and held returns per unit of risk flat — but it was not free: 8bps of NIM went to competition and deposit mix, jaws were slightly negative, and the NPL stock rose materially. The credit deterioration sits in the stock, not the FY25 charge, and the 2H25 impaired spike is substantially two Agri single names.

| B&PB (restated) | FY25 | FY24 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| GLAs | $279.5bn | $261.7bn | +6.8% |
| — Business lending | $166.3bn | $155.0bn | +7.3% |
| Net operating income | $8,531m | $8,358m | +2.1% |
| Cash earnings | $3,330m | $3,277m | +1.6% |
| NIM | 3.01% | 3.09% | −8bps |
| CIC / GLAs | 0.19% | 0.20% | −1bp |
| Cash earnings / avg RWA | 2.18% | 2.19% | −1bp |
| Cost to income | 37.9% | 37.6% | +30bps |
| Impaired / GLAs | 0.49% | 0.39% | +10bps |
| Default-not-impaired / GLAs | 2.05% | 1.74% | +31bps |

(Results book, PDF p.36)

**Reconciliation.** Volume did the work: average interest-earning assets +5.4% converted to NII of only +2.8% because NIM gave up 8bps to "competitive pressures impacting both the business and housing lending portfolios, as well as higher deposit costs" (results book p.37). The margin stabilised in 2H25 (3.01%→3.02%). Other income fell 2.9% (of which $22m was the NZ wealth disposal). Costs +2.9% (bankers, technology) left underlying profit +1.6%; the CIC rose only $6m, so cash earnings also grew 1.6%. Deposits +6.6% to $237.9bn broadly funded the $17.8bn of lending growth.

**Margin vs credit as the price of growth.** The P&L credit cost did not rise with volume: CIC/GLAs fell 1bp to 0.19%, and the business-lending charge fell YoY ($209m+$308m halves in FY24 vs $165m+$266m in FY25 — presentation p.95); the FY25 increase was housing. The stock deteriorated: B&PB NPEs reached $7,079m, 2.54% of GLAs (2.12% Sep 24), and business-lending NPLs 3.22% of business GLAs (2.66%). RWA grew 9.0% — faster than GLAs — partly from "deterioration in asset quality", yet cash earnings/avg RWA held at 2.18% and combined Business Banking ROE is disclosed at 18%.

**Broad-based vs single-name.** Growth: broad-based — "business lending across a broad range of sectors" (results book p.24); Agri +3.5%, Health +5.9%, CRE +7.4%, Other +10.4%, small business +9.2%; SME share up to 28.0% (presentation p.50). Deterioration: the FY-long default-not-impaired build (+31bps) is portfolio-wide, but the Sep-25 impaired spike is single-name-skewed — two large, well-secured Agri customers add 21bps to the 3.22% NPL ratio, excluding which the ratio fell 3bps HoH to 3.01%; watch loans fell 9bps, the first decline since Mar 23 (presentation p.26-27). Underwriting looks held: 73% fully secured, 6% unsecured, sub-investment-grade share 77% vs 78% (presentation p.95).

**Net:** value-accretive growth at broadly flat risk-adjusted returns, with modest margin/cost dilution — not growth bought with credit standards.

Confidence: 80/100.

key_facts.fact: B&PB gross loans and acceptances grew 6.8% to $279.5bn in FY25, with business lending up 7.3% to $166.3bn and housing up 5.8% to $109.3bn.

citations.quote: Housing lending 109.3 103.3 5.8 ... Business lending 166.3 155.0 7.3 ... Gross loans and acceptances 279.5 261.7 6.8

key_facts.fact: B&PB net operating income rose 2.1% to $8,531m and cash earnings rose 1.6% to $3,330m, so revenue and earnings grew far slower than volumes.

citations.quote: Net operating income 8,531 8,358 2.1
Cash earnings increased by $53 million or 1.6%, driven by higher net operating income, partially offset by higher operating expenses and modestly higher credit impairment charges.

key_facts.fact: B&PB NIM fell 8bps to 3.01% in FY25 due to lending competition and deposit costs, but rose 1bp half-on-half in 2H25.

citations.quote: Net interest margin 3.01 3.09 (8 bps) 3.02 3.01 1 bp

Net interest margin decreased by 8 basis points reflecting competitive pressures impacting both the business and housing lending portfolios, as well as higher deposit costs including mix impacts due to term deposit growth.

key_facts.fact: B&PB average interest earning assets rose 5.4% ($12.8bn), converting to net interest income growth of only 2.8% ($204m) after the margin decline.

citations.quote: Average interest earning assets increased by $12.8 billion or 5.4% reflecting growth in both business and housing lending.
Net interest income 7,499 7,295 2.8

key_facts.fact: The B&PB credit impairment charge rose only $6m (1.1%) to $529m, and CIC to GLAs fell 1bp to 0.19%; the increase was housing-driven, with business lending charges lower year on year.

citations.quote: Credit impairment charge (529) (523) 1.1 ... Credit impairment charge to GLAs - annualised 0.19 0.20 (1 bp)
The increase mainly reflects a higher charge for home lending, partially offset by a lower charge for business lending.

key_facts.fact: By half, B&PB business-lending impairment charges were $209m/$308m in FY24 versus $165m/$266m in FY25, while housing charges swung from write-backs to $37m/$16m.

citations.quote: 209 308 165 266 (1) (7) Mar 24 (6) 20 Sep 24 37 35 Mar 25 16 10 Sep 25 201 322 237 292 Housing lending Business lending Other banking products

key_facts.fact: B&PB asset-quality stock metrics deteriorated over FY25: impaired assets to GLAs +10bps to 0.49% and default-but-not-impaired +31bps to 2.05%.

citations.quote: Impaired assets to GLAs 0.49 0.39 10 bps Default but not impaired assets to GLAs(3) 2.05 1.74 31 bps

key_facts.fact: B&PB non-performing exposures rose to $7,079m or 2.54% of GLAs at Sep 25 from $5,580m or 2.12% at Sep 24; business-lending NPLs reached 3.22% of business GLAs versus 2.66%.

The Sep-25 spike in the B&PB business-lending NPL ratio is substantially two single names: two large well-secured Agri customers account for 21bps, and excluding them the ratio fell 3bps half-on-half to 3.01%.

citations.quote: Excluding two large well secured Agri customers, underlying NPL ratio down 3bps to 3.01%
Includes 21bps relating to 2 large Agri customers
Uplift in NPL ratio during 2H25 mainly due to customer specific issues for two large well secured customers

key_facts.fact: The half-on-half rise in default-but-not-impaired assets was driven by a small number of large Agriculture downgrades in B&PB, and group-wide single names sat in C&IB and NZ Banking.

citations.quote: partially offset by the downgrade of a small number of large customers in the Agriculture portfolio in Business and Private Banking.
Business lending single names impacting impaired ratio and individually assessed charges (C&IB, NZ Banking)

key_facts.fact: Lending growth was broad-based, not concentrated: business lending grew across a broad range of sectors, with Agri +3.5%, Health +5.9%, CRE +7.4%, Other +10.4% and small business +9.2%, and SME market share rose to 28.0%.

citations.quote: an increase of $11.8 billion or 7.4% in Business and Private Banking driven by growth in business lending across a broad range of sectors.
Broad based growth across most sectors including Trade, Manufacturing, Construction, Transport
3.5% 5.9% 7.4% 10.4% 7.3% 9.2% Agri Health CRE Other NAB B&PB NAB Small business 27.8% 27.7% 27.8% 28.0%

key_facts.fact: Underwriting settings look held rather than loosened: the business book stayed 73% fully secured and 6% unsecured, and the sub-investment-grade-equivalent share edged down to 77% from 78%.

citations.quote: 75% 74% 73% 73% 19% 20% 21% 21% 6% 6% 6% 6% Mar 24 Sep 24 Mar 25 Sep 25 Fully Secured Partially Secured Unsecured 77% 78% 78% 77%

key_facts.fact: Group watch loans fell 9bps to 1.17% of GLAs in 2H25, the first half-yearly reduction since Mar 23, supporting a stabilising underlying credit trend.

citations.quote: First half-yearly reduction in watch loans since Mar 23

key_facts.fact: Growth consumed capital faster than it earned: B&PB RWA rose 9.0% ($13.2bn), partly from asset-quality deterioration, yet cash earnings on average RWA held at 2.18% (down 1bp) and cash earnings on average assets fell 5bps to 1.25%.

citations.quote: The increase in risk-weighted assets was mostly due to growth in business lending volumes, combined with deterioration in asset quality.
Cash earnings on average assets 1.25 1.30 (5 bps) ... Cash earnings on average risk-weighted assets 2.18 2.19 (1 bp)

key_facts.fact: Growth was largely self-funded and jaws slightly negative: customer deposits grew 6.6% to $237.9bn, operating expenses rose 2.9% and the cost to income ratio rose 30bps to 37.9%.

citations.quote: Customer deposits 237.9 223.1 6.6 ... Operating expenses(2) (3,232) (3,141) 2.9 ... Cost to income ratio 37.9 37.6 30 bps

key_facts.fact: Combined Business Banking (B&PB plus C&IB) is disclosed at an 18% FY25 ROE on stated assumptions, supporting returns-accretive growth at the business-bank level.

citations.quote: Combined Business Banking 18% ROE
FY25 ROE for B&PB and C&IB combined, based on cash earnings/average RWA and 11.25% CET1 ratio, excludes centrally held RWA and deductions

key_facts.fact: Group collective provisions for the B&PB business book rose for both volume growth and asset-quality deterioration, and individually assessed provisions were raised for the B&PB business lending portfolio.

citations.quote: an increase in provisions held for the Business and Private Banking business lending portfolio due to volume growth and deterioration in asset quality

Individually assessed provisions increased by $407 million or 53.8% to $1,163 million, primarily driven by new and increased provisions raised for: • the business lending portfolio in Business and Private Banking

limitations: NAB discloses no standalone B&PB ROE; the 18% ROE is B&PB and C&IB combined on stated capital assumptions, so B&PB-only return on capital cannot be isolated.
The split of the $529m B&PB credit impairment charge between individually assessed and collective components is not printed at divisional level.
Sector-level B&PB NPL ratios (presentation p.27) are charted without printed values, so the depth of deterioration per sector cannot be quantified from the documents.
The dollar exposure of the two large Agri customers is not disclosed; only their 21bps impact on the business-lending NPL ratio is given.
Front-book versus back-book lending spreads for B&PB are not disclosed, so the pricing of new growth cannot be measured directly; the NIM bridge detail is group-level only.
FY24 comparatives are restated for PB/B&PB portfolio transfers and an expense re-presentation; growth rates can only be assessed on the restated basis.
Expected loss content of the higher NPL stock is not disclosed by division; provision coverage of B&PB NPEs specifically is not printed.
